meta.title: Water Heater Advisor — Brand and Product Selection Research
rules: Do not size tankless from headline maximum GPM. Use verified flow at design temperature rise.
Do not publish blanket warranty terms. Store model/line, component, use case, recirculation condition, installation condition, source and checked date.
Do not call a contractor authorized/certified/trained unless that exact status is supported by the manufacturer's current directory or program record.
Do not use budget to select a brand unless current local price evidence exists.
Unknown is preferable to invented precision.
important_corrections: Navien is no longer tankless-only in the U.S. residential market; the NWP500 heat-pump line is current.
Rinnai currently sells gas tankless and electric heat-pump water heaters in the U.S.; its FAQ says it does not make electric tankless water heaters.
Noritz has enough current residential and Central Valley relevance to be added to the quiz's gas-tankless brand preferences.
Bradford White technically has current electric tankless products, but the current TEF/TET KwickShot products are point-of-use/fixed-fixture products, not a clean whole-home peer to gas tankless.
Rheem and A. O. Smith both have current 120V heat-pump options that can change conversion feasibility.

brand_technology_matrix.notes: Current U.S. residential water-heater catalog lists multiple gas tankless families and NWP500 HPWH. No current residential storage-tank family found.

brand_technology_matrix.primary_strength: Broad gas-tankless portfolio, current RX/RXP platform, strong recirculation options, and current REHP heat-pump line.
brand_technology_matrix.notes: Rinnai's own FAQ states that it does not make an electric tankless model. Current U.S. residential site shows tankless and REHP heat-pump water heaters.

brand_technology_matrix.primary_strength: The broadest technology coverage in the priority set, including 120V and 240V heat-pump options and whole-home/point-of-use electric tankless.
brand_technology_matrix.notes: Current Rheem residential water-heating catalog contains tank, gas tankless, electric tankless and heat-pump products.

brand_technology_matrix.primary_strength: Very broad technology coverage, Adapt tankless, 120V Voltex HPWH, and a new Voltex X outdoor split HPWH.

then.reason: Never revive a technically eliminated technology because of brand preference.
Explain that the preferred brand does not offer the selected technology and continue with compatible brands.
Size from verified flow at design temperature rise, not headline maximum GPM.
NPE-240A2 provides 11.2 GPM at 35F rise, 8.7 at 45F, and 5.6 at 67F; use the design-rise point.
Use Rinnai's inlet-temperature sizing table; e.g. RX/RXP199 is about 5.7 GPM at 52F inlet and 120F setpoint.
EZ111 must pass its verified rise curve: 7.8 GPM at 50F rise, 6.5 at 60F, 5.6 at 70F, 4.9 at 80F.
EZ98 must pass its verified rise curve: 6.9 GPM at 50F rise, 5.7 at 60F, 4.9 at 70F.
EZ71 should only be recommended where its verified design-rise flow meets simultaneous demand.
Use 5.9 GPM at 67F rise for ATHR-199X3 planning rather than the 10.5 GPM headline maximum.
Treat 1/2-inch compatibility as conditional. Require actual gas-load/pressure/length sizing before preferring a brand.
Compare the actual vent route to the exact model's allowed material, diameter, equivalent length and termination rules.
Prefer a verified pump-integrated line when it fits the loop and demand: NPE-A2, RXP, IKONIC SR/RTG-R, or NRCR are examples.

avoid_brands: Navien NPE-A2 in uncontrolled recirculation configuration
then.reason: Uncontrolled recirculation cuts NPE-A2 residential heat-exchanger coverage from 15 years to 5 years and parts from 5 to 3.
Boost EZ Pro/EZTR because the current line is explicitly designed around storage-tank replacement.
EZ Pro's top water connections can reduce repiping in some tank replacements.
Only recommend exact models/configurations explicitly approved for outdoor installation or with the required outdoor kit.
Exclude any model whose verified GPM at design rise is below calculated simultaneous demand, regardless of brand.
Use exact model minimum firing rate/activation flow as a tie-breaker for low-demand homes; do not apply a brand-wide assumption.
Give a small preference to X3 where scale protection matters, but label its longevity benefit as a manufacturer claim, not independent reliability proof.
Penalize tankless technology where maintenance willingness is low; do not solve a technology-level mismatch by switching brands.
Strongly penalize or exclude a brand when qualified local service cannot be verified, especially for urgent or complex equipment.
Rinnai has a current ACE PRO record in Modesto, which is a routing/service signal, not proof the product is superior.
Noritz's current Modesto-area directory shows multiple installers/servicers and a contractor explicitly labeled Noritz trained.
Use the current A.O. Smith Modesto manufacturer locator as a positive routing signal; re-check status at routing time.
Rheem's current Modesto directory shows multiple contractors under heat-pump water heating.
Shortlist current 120V HPWHs, then size by FHR and location; do not force a 208/240V brand preference.
NWP500 requires at least 450 cu ft for unvented installation or ducting for enclosed spaces.
Voltex X's outdoor split architecture can solve indoor air-volume/heat-extraction constraints that unitary HPWHs cannot.
Compare exact first-hour rating after electrical/location feasibility; gallon label alone is insufficient.
Require the installation location to fit the exact model's heat-pump operating range and understand when resistance backup takes over.
Let technology selection favor HPWH first; brand is chosen only after circuit, FHR, location and service checks.
Give only a small tie-breaker bonus when same-brand replacement demonstrably reduces connections, venting, controls, parts or service complexity.
Bradford White's professional/wholesale channel makes it a weaker fit for a homeowner who insists on direct retail/self-sourcing.
Keep Bradford White only when local professional supply/service is verified; Ferguson's Modesto presence is positive but exact part stock must be checked.
Do not add electric tankless as a standard fifth technology until service amperage, panel capacity, circuit count and design-rise demand are collected.

avoid_brands: A. O. Smith high-power electric tankless
then.reason: A.O. Smith says its larger electric-tankless models can draw up to about 135A; insufficient panel/service capacity is a hard exclusion.

avoid_brands: Bradford White KwickShot TEF/TET as whole-home default
then.reason: Current KwickShot TEF/TET products are point-of-use/fixed-fixture products; old broader ES/EFC/EFT family is discontinued.
Favor a compatible in-stock like-for-like tank first; choose brand by exact FHR, dimensions, vent/electrical fit, stock and service.
Use 'authorized', 'certified', 'trained', 'ACE PRO', 'NSS' or equivalent only when the current manufacturer source shows that exact status.
Do not reject a Navien preference merely because HPWH was selected; NWP500 is now a current 50/65/80-gal residential HPWH line. It still must pass circuit, air-volume and FHR gates.

verified_diagnostic_evidence: NPE-A2 FAQ says no-hot-water with no error code may be caused by a flow sensor not spinning, including debris as a possible contributor.
reliability_and_failure_modes.notes: Manufacturer troubleshooting evidence is not a prevalence study. Do not label the flow sensor as the brand's 'common failure' without field data.

verified_diagnostic_evidence: Current tankless diagnostic guide includes Code 25 for condensate pump error or clogged/frozen drain on applicable products.
reliability_and_failure_modes.notes: Error-code documentation describes failure categories, not how frequently they occur.

verified_diagnostic_evidence: Current HPWH manual includes compressor/airflow/temperature/dry-fire alarm categories.
Rheem's 2026 maintenance guidance says dirty HPWH air filters can contribute to error codes, reduced efficiency and wear.
reliability_and_failure_modes.notes: Do not convert service-manual diagnostic categories into reliability rankings.

verified_diagnostic_evidence: A.O. Smith University publishes current training for tankless codes including 031, 111/121, 391, 441, 711 and 991/101.
reliability_and_failure_modes.notes: The existence of training for a code does not establish prevalence. X3 longevity claims must be labeled manufacturer_claim.

verified_diagnostic_evidence: Noritz Code 90 means combustion/airflow abnormality. For new installs the manufacturer points to gas supply, venting, condensate and configuration; on established units it also points to dirt/maintenance and condensate blockage.
reliability_and_failure_modes.notes: Noritz itself uses 'could' and context-specific causes. Do not make Code 90 a brand-reliability claim.

verified_diagnostic_evidence: Current Infiniti GR/GS manuals include water-temperature, fan, venting, leak-detection, flame and gas-system diagnostic codes.
reliability_and_failure_modes.notes: No defensible current comparative failure-rate or problem-year dataset was found.

head_to_head.choose_ao_smith_when: Voltex 120 has the better FHR/circuit fit, or Voltex X solves an indoor-space/air constraint that a unitary HPWH does not.

historical_recall_records.interpretation: Relevant to legacy-unit identification in California, not a current-line reliability ranking.

gas_tankless.planning_baseline: about 20 years is a common technology-level planning figure
gas_tankless.notes: Actual life depends heavily on installation, water quality, maintenance, duty cycle and repairability.

storage_tank.planning_baseline: roughly 10-15 years is a common technology-level planning range
storage_tank.notes: Do not use this to rank the six brands.

heat_pump.planning_baseline: similar broad lifespan category to electric storage; many current products carry 10-year tank/parts coverage
heat_pump.notes: Warranty length is not the same as expected service life.
